If the fabric has a width of $1\,\frac{1}{2}\,\text{m},$ what will be the area of the tablecloth? Express your answer as a **mixed number** in simplest form. The tablecloth will have an area of {{field-1}} ${\text{m}}^{2}.$" :question/worked-solution "The tablecloth will have an area of $(2\,\frac{1}{4}\times 1\,\frac{1}{2}){\text{m}}^{2}.$ First, we write $2\,\frac{1}{4}$ as an improper fraction: $$ 2\,\frac{1}{4}=\frac{(2\times 4)+1}{4}=\frac{9}{4} $$ We also write $1\,\frac{1}{2}$ as an improper fraction: $$ 1\,\frac{1}{2}=\frac{(1\times 2)+1}{2}=\frac{3}{2} $$ Now, we can multiply the two numbers. We multiply the numerators, and we multiply the denominators: $$ \frac{9}{4}\times \frac{3}{2}=\frac{9\times 3}{4\times 2}=\frac{27}{8} $$ Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number: $$ \frac{27}{8}=3\,\text{R}3=3\,\frac{3}{8}. $$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-10ea190f-2b81-55d5-aae9-2f2c1fbbbaf2"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-10ea190f-2b81-55d5-aae9-2f2c1fbbbaf2" :answer-field/id #uuid "10ea190f-2b81-55d5-aae9-2f2c1fbbbaf2" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-80e8c721-00c6-52fa-9c87-aa630d796ce8" :answer-field/choices ["answer-80e8c721-00c6-52fa-9c87-aa630d796ce8"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-80e8c721-00c6-52fa-9c87-aa630d796ce8" :answer/id #uuid "80e8c721-00c6-52fa-9c87-aa630d796ce8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3\frac{3}{8}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186138377 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-d13eae43-32e2-575a-85c2-71abf6bbd783"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-d13eae43-32e2-575a-85c2-71abf6bbd783" :question/id #uuid "d13eae43-32e2-575a-85c2-71abf6bbd783" :question/math-academy-id "q-166774" :question/problem "Carmen cuts two pieces of drill fabric with lengths of $\frac{5}{6}\,\text{m}$ and $\frac{9}{7}\,\text{m}.$ The sum of the lengths of the two pieces of fabric is{{field-1}}$\text{m}.$" :question/worked-solution "The sum of the lengths of the two pieces of fabric is $(\frac{5}{6}+\frac{9}{7})\text{m}.$ To add two fractions with unlike denominators, we need to express each fraction as an equivalent fraction with a common denominator. Let's look at the denominators: $$ \frac{5}{6}+\frac{9}{7} $$ The least common denominator of $6$ and $7$ is $42.$ To put $\frac{5}{6}$ over a denominator of $42,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $7:$ $$ \frac{5}{6}=\frac{5\times 7}{6\times 7}=\frac{35}{42} $$ To put $\frac{9}{7}$ over a denominator of $42,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $6:$ $$ \frac{9}{7}=\frac{9\times 6}{7\times 6}=\frac{54}{42} $$ We can now add the fractions. We keep the denominator the same, and we add the numerators. $$ \frac{35}{42}+\frac{54}{42}=\frac{89}{42} $$ Expressing this fraction as a mixed number, we get $$ \frac{89}{42}=2\,\frac{5}{42}. $$ Therefore, the sum of the lengths of the two pieces of fabric is $2\,\frac{5}{42}\,\text{m}.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-d8ed4fae-048d-5f03-b27c-895a7582dfc5"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-d8ed4fae-048d-5f03-b27c-895a7582dfc5" :answer-field/id #uuid "d8ed4fae-048d-5f03-b27c-895a7582dfc5" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-8a68bafd-e384-5f9b-83b4-e06cb2184c8c" :answer-field/choices ["answer-8a68bafd-e384-5f9b-83b4-e06cb2184c8c"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8a68bafd-e384-5f9b-83b4-e06cb2184c8c" :answer/id #uuid "8a68bafd-e384-5f9b-83b4-e06cb2184c8c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{89}{42}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186138577 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-86788b5f-c043-547d-a152-64c87d27af72"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-86788b5f-c043-547d-a152-64c87d27af72" :question/id #uuid "86788b5f-c043-547d-a152-64c87d27af72" :question/math-academy-id "q-166775" :question/problem "Carmen has a piece of fabric with a length of $5\,\frac{1}{4}\,\text{m}.$ She accidentally spills coffee on this piece, so she decides to cut out and discard $1\,\frac{1}{5}\,\text{m}$ of fabric. How long is the remaining piece of fabric? Express your answer as a **mixed number** in simplest form. The remaining piece of fabric has a length of {{field-1}} $\text{m}.$" :question/worked-solution "The new piece of fabric has a length of $(5\,\frac{1}{4}-1\,\frac{1}{5})\text{m}$ long. To subtract two mixed numbers, we subtract whole numbers from whole numbers and fractions from fractions. Subtracting the whole numbers, we get $5-1=4.$ Now we subtract the fractions: $$ \frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5} $$ Let's look at the denominators. The least common denominator of $4$ and $5$ is $20.$ To put $\frac{1}{4}$ over a denominator of $20,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $5:$ $$ \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1\times 5}{4\times 5}=\frac{5}{20} $$ To put $\frac{1}{5}$ over a denominator of $20,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $4:$ $$ \frac{1}{5}=\frac{1\times 4}{5\times 4}=\frac{4}{20} $$ We can now subtract the fractions. We keep the denominator the same, and we subtract the numerators: $$ \frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5}=\frac{5}{20}-\frac{4}{20}=\frac{1}{20} $$ Therefore, $$ 5\,\frac{1}{4}-1\,\frac{1}{5}=4\,\frac{1}{20}. $$" The tablecloth will have an area of {{field-1}} ${\text{m}}^{2}.$" :question/worked-solution "The tablecloth will have an area of $(2\,\frac{1}{4}\times 1\,\frac{1}{2}){\text{m}}^{2}.$ First, we write $2\,\frac{1}{4}$ as an improper fraction: $$ 2\,\frac{1}{4}=\frac{(2\times 4)+1}{4}=\frac{9}{4} $$ We also write $1\,\frac{1}{2}$ as an improper fraction: $$ 1\,\frac{1}{2}=\frac{(1\times 2)+1}{2}=\frac{3}{2} $$ Now, we can multiply the two numbers. We multiply the numerators, and we multiply the denominators: $$ \frac{9}{4}\times \frac{3}{2}=\frac{9\times 3}{4\times 2}=\frac{27}{8} $$ Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number: $$ \frac{27}{8}=3\,\text{R}3=3\,\frac{3}{8}. $$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-10ea190f-2b81-55d5-aae9-2f2c1fbbbaf2"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-10ea190f-2b81-55d5-aae9-2f2c1fbbbaf2" :answer-field/id #uuid "10ea190f-2b81-55d5-aae9-2f2c1fbbbaf2" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-80e8c721-00c6-52fa-9c87-aa630d796ce8" :answer-field/choices ["answer-80e8c721-00c6-52fa-9c87-aa630d796ce8"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-80e8c721-00c6-52fa-9c87-aa630d796ce8" :answer/id #uuid "80e8c721-00c6-52fa-9c87-aa630d796ce8" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3\frac{3}{8}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186138377 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-d13eae43-32e2-575a-85c2-71abf6bbd783"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-d13eae43-32e2-575a-85c2-71abf6bbd783" :question/id #uuid "d13eae43-32e2-575a-85c2-71abf6bbd783" :question/math-academy-id "q-166774" :question/problem "Carmen cuts two pieces of drill fabric with lengths of $\frac{5}{6}\,\text{m}$ and $\frac{9}{7}\,\text{m}.$ The sum of the lengths of the two pieces of fabric is{{field-1}}$\text{m}.$" :question/worked-solution "The sum of the lengths of the two pieces of fabric is $(\frac{5}{6}+\frac{9}{7})\text{m}.$ To add two fractions with unlike denominators, we need to express each fraction as an equivalent fraction with a common denominator. Let's look at the denominators: $$ \frac{5}{6}+\frac{9}{7} $$ The least common denominator of $6$ and $7$ is $42.$ To put $\frac{5}{6}$ over a denominator of $42,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $7:$ $$ \frac{5}{6}=\frac{5\times 7}{6\times 7}=\frac{35}{42} $$ To put $\frac{9}{7}$ over a denominator of $42,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $6:$ $$ \frac{9}{7}=\frac{9\times 6}{7\times 6}=\frac{54}{42} $$ We can now add the fractions. We keep the denominator the same, and we add the numerators. $$ \frac{35}{42}+\frac{54}{42}=\frac{89}{42} $$ Expressing this fraction as a mixed number, we get $$ \frac{89}{42}=2\,\frac{5}{42}. $$ Therefore, the sum of the lengths of the two pieces of fabric is $2\,\frac{5}{42}\,\text{m}.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate :question/answer-fields ["answer-field-d8ed4fae-048d-5f03-b27c-895a7582dfc5"] :db/ensure [:question/validate]} {:db/id "answer-field-d8ed4fae-048d-5f03-b27c-895a7582dfc5" :answer-field/id #uuid "d8ed4fae-048d-5f03-b27c-895a7582dfc5" :answer-field/key "field-1" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank :answer-field/correct "answer-8a68bafd-e384-5f9b-83b4-e06cb2184c8c" :answer-field/choices ["answer-8a68bafd-e384-5f9b-83b4-e06cb2184c8c"] :db/ensure [:answer-field/validate]} {:db/id "answer-8a68bafd-e384-5f9b-83b4-e06cb2184c8c" :answer/id #uuid "8a68bafd-e384-5f9b-83b4-e06cb2184c8c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{89}{42}" :db/ensure [:answer/validate]} {:db/id 17592186138577 :knowledge-point/questions ["question-86788b5f-c043-547d-a152-64c87d27af72"] :db/ensure [:knowledge-point/validate]} {:db/id "question-86788b5f-c043-547d-a152-64c87d27af72" :question/id #uuid "86788b5f-c043-547d-a152-64c87d27af72" :question/math-academy-id "q-166775" :question/problem "Carmen has a piece of fabric with a length of $5\,\frac{1}{4}\,\text{m}.$ She accidentally spills coffee on this piece, so she decides to cut out and discard $1\,\frac{1}{5}\,\text{m}$ of fabric. Subtracting the whole numbers, we get $5-1=4.$ Now we subtract the fractions: $$ \frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5} $$ Let's look at the denominators. The least common denominator of $4$ and $5$ is $20.$ To put $\frac{1}{4}$ over a denominator of $20,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $5:$ $$ \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1\times 5}{4\times 5}=\frac{5}{20} $$ To put $\frac{1}{5}$ over a denominator of $20,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $4:$ $$ \frac{1}{5}=\frac{1\times 4}{5\times 4}=\frac{4}{20} $$ We can now subtract the fractions. We keep the denominator the same, and we subtract the numerators: $$ \frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5}=\frac{5}{20}-\frac{4}{20}=\frac{1}{20} $$ Therefore, $$ 5\,\frac{1}{4}-1\,\frac{1}{5}=4\,\frac{1}{20}. $$" :question/worked-solution "The sum of the lengths of the two pieces of fabric is $(\frac{5}{6}+\frac{9}{7})\text{m}.$ To add two fractions with unlike denominators, we need to express each fraction as an equivalent fraction with a common denominator. Let's look at the denominators: $$ \frac{5}{6}+\frac{9}{7} $$ The least common denominator of $6$ and $7$ is $42.$ To put $\frac{5}{6}$ over a denominator of $42,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $7:$ $$ \frac{5}{6}=\frac{5\times 7}{6\times 7}=\frac{35}{42} $$ To put $\frac{9}{7}$ over a denominator of $42,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $6:$ $$ \frac{9}{7}=\frac{9\times 6}{7\times 6}=\frac{54}{42} $$ We can now add the fractions. We keep the denominator the same, and we add the numerators. $$ \frac{35}{42}+\frac{54}{42}=\frac{89}{42} $$ Expressing this fraction as a mixed number, we get $$ \frac{89}{42}=2\,\frac{5}{42}. $$ Therefore, the sum of the lengths of the two pieces of fabric is $2\,\frac{5}{42}\,\text{m}.$"] ["question-d13eae43-32e2-575a-85c2-71abf6bbd783" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] ["answer-field-d8ed4fae-048d-5f03-b27c-895a7582dfc5" :answer-field/id #uuid "d8ed4fae-048d-5f03-b27c-895a7582dfc5"] ["answer-8a68bafd-e384-5f9b-83b4-e06cb2184c8c" :answer/id #uuid "8a68bafd-e384-5f9b-83b4-e06cb2184c8c"] ["answer-8a68bafd-e384-5f9b-83b4-e06cb2184c8c" :answer/type :answer.type/math] ["answer-8a68bafd-e384-5f9b-83b4-e06cb2184c8c" :answer/value "\frac{89}{42}"] ["answer-field-d8ed4fae-048d-5f03-b27c-895a7582dfc5" :answer-field/key "field-1"] ["answer-field-d8ed4fae-048d-5f03-b27c-895a7582dfc5" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/blank] ["answer-field-d8ed4fae-048d-5f03-b27c-895a7582dfc5" :answer-field/correct "answer-8a68bafd-e384-5f9b-83b4-e06cb2184c8c"] ["answer-field-d8ed4fae-048d-5f03-b27c-895a7582dfc5" :answer-field/choices "answer-8a68bafd-e384-5f9b-83b4-e06cb2184c8c"] ["question-d13eae43-32e2-575a-85c2-71abf6bbd783" :question/answer-fields "answer-field-d8ed4fae-048d-5f03-b27c-895a7582dfc5"] [17592186138377 :knowledge-point/questions "question-d13eae43-32e2-575a-85c2-71abf6bbd783"] ["question-86788b5f-c043-547d-a152-64c87d27af72" :question/id #uuid "86788b5f-c043-547d-a152-64c87d27af72"] ["question-86788b5f-c043-547d-a152-64c87d27af72" :question/math-academy-id "q-166775"] ["question-86788b5f-c043-547d-a152-64c87d27af72" :question/problem "Carmen has a piece of fabric with a length of $5\,\frac{1}{4}\,\text{m}.$ She accidentally spills coffee on this piece, so she decides to cut out and discard $1\,\frac{1}{5}\,\text{m}$ of fabric. Subtracting the whole numbers, we get $5-1=4.$ Now we subtract the fractions: $$ \frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{5} $$ Let's look at the denominators. The least common denominator of $4$ and $5$ is $20.$ To put $\frac{1}{4}$ over a denominator of $20,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $5:$ $$ \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1\times 5}{4\times 5}=\frac{5}{20} $$ To put $\frac{1}{5}$ over a denominator of $20,$ we multiply the numerator and denominator by $4:$ $$ \frac{1}{5}=\frac{1\times 4}{5\times 4}=\frac{4}{20} $$ We can now subtract the fractions. how to use a box model by finding the value of $300 \\div 25$.\n\nWe start by writing our division in the following way. We place the dividend in a box and the divisor to the left of the box.\n\n|  |  |  |  |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| $25$ | $3$$0$$0$ |  |  |\n\nWe want to find how many times $25$ goes into $300$. But instead of trying to figure this out in a single step, let's break this problem up into a series of simpler steps.\n\nIn our first step, we will pick a multiple of $25$ that is easy to compute and is fairly large but no larger than $300$. We will choose the multiple $25 \\times {\\color{blue}10}$ because we can compute\n\n$$\n25 \\times {\\color{blue}10} = 250\n$$\n\nquickly and the result is no larger than $300$.\n\nTo organize our work so far, we write $\\color{blue}10$ above the box and subtract $25 \\times {\\color{blue}10}$ from $300$ inside the box.\n\n|  | $\\color{blue}10$ |  |  |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| $25$ | $3$$0$$0$$-\\!$$2$$5$$0$$\\color{red}5$$\\color{red}0$ |  |  |\n\nThe result of the subtraction is ${\\color{red}50}$. This indicates that if we take $25$ a total of ${\\color{blue}10}$ times, then it will fit into $300$ with $\\color{red}50$ left over.\n\nNow, we repeat the process with a dividend of $\\color{red}50$ instead of $300$. To start the next round, we write $\\color{red}50$ in a new box to the right.\n\n|  | $10$ |  |  |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| $25$ | $3$$0$$0$$-\\!\\!\\!$$2$$5$$0$$\\color{red}5$$\\color{red}0$ | $\\color{red}5$$\\color{red}0$ |  |\n\nAgain, we are looking for a multiple of $25$ that is easy to compute and is no larger than ${\\color{red}50}$. before, we write $\\color{blue}2$ above the box and subtract $25 \\times {\\color{blue}2}$ from ${\\color{red}50}$ inside the box.\n\n|  | $10$ | $\\color{blue}2$ |  |\n| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |\n| $25$ | $3$$0$$0$$-\\!$$2$$5$$0$$\\color{red}5$$\\color{red}0$ | $\\color{red}5$$\\color{red}0$$-\\!\\!\\!$$5$$0$$\\fbox{0}$ |  |\n\nWe get $\\fbox{0}$, so the division is done.\n\nTo find the quotient do we find the value of\n\n$$\n\\dfrac{2}{{\\color{red}{3}}} + \\dfrac 1 {\\color{blue}6}\n$$\n\nwithout using a fraction model?\n\nThe denominators are $\\color{red}3$ and $\\color{blue}6$, which are So to add the fractions, we need to find a common denominator.\n\nNotice that ${\\color{blue}{6}}$ is a multiple of ${\\color{red}{3}}$. The multiples of ${\\color{red}{3}}$ are:\n\n$$\n\\quad 3, {\\color{blue}{6}}, 9, 12, \\ldots\n$$\n\nTherefore, the least common denominator is ${\\color{blue}{6}}$.\n\nWe can put\n\n$$\n\\dfrac{2}{\\color{red}3}\n$$\n\nover a denominator of $\\color{blue}6$ by multiplying the numerator and denominator by $2$:\n\n$$\n\\dfrac{2}{\\color{red}{3}} = \\dfrac{2\\times2}{{\\color{red}{3}}\\times 2} = \\dfrac{4}{\\color{blue}{6}}\n$$\n\nWe don't need to do anything to\n\n$$\n\\dfrac{1}{\\color{blue}6}\n$$\n\nsince it already has a denominator of ${\\color{blue}6}$.\n\nNow, we can add the fractions:\n\n$$\n\\frac{4}{6} + \\frac{1}{6} = \\frac{5}{6}\n$$\n\nAnd that's our answer!\n\nWe would have gotten the same answer using a fraction model, "1590b647-48b6-549e-9979-e9b3eb563f55" :step/math-academy-id 134959 :step/next {:db/id 17592186139275}} {:db/id 17592186139275 :step/content {:db/id 17592186139700 :tutorial/content "When adding fractions, if one denominator is not a multiple of the other, we can always find a common denominator by multiplying the denominators together.\n\nFor example, let's find the value of\n\n$$\n\\dfrac{1}{\\color{red}2}+\\dfrac{1}{\\color{blue}3}\n$$\n\nNotice that $\\color{red}2$ is not a multiple of ${\\color{blue}{3}}$ and vice-versa. However, an easy common denominator is\n\n$$\n{\\color{red}2}\\times {\\color{blue}3} = 6\n$$\n\nTo put\n\n$$\n\\dfrac 1 {\\color{red}{2}}\n$$\n\nover a denominator of $6$, we multiply the numerator and denominator by ${\\color{blue}3}$:\n\n$$\n\\dfrac{1}{{\\color{red}{2}}} = \\dfrac{1\\times {\\color{blue}{3}}}{{\\color{red}{2}} \\times {\\color{blue}{3}}} = \\dfrac{3}{6}\n$$\n\nTo put\n\n$$\n\\dfrac 1 {\\color{blue}{3}}\n$$\n\nover a denominator of $6$, we multiply the numerator and denominator by ${\\color{red}{2}}$:\n\n$$\n\\dfrac{1}{{\\color{blue}{3}}} = \\dfrac{1\\times {\\color{red}{2}}}{{\\color{blue}{3}} \\times {\\color{red}{2}}} = \\dfrac{2}{6}\n$$\n\nWe can now add the fractions. We keep the denominator the same, and we add the numerators.\n\n$$\n\\frac{3}{6} + \\frac{2}{6} = \\frac{5}{6}\n$$\n\nAnd we're done!\n\nNotice that the fraction model gives us the same result:\n\n![](images/f2/f2704054fbbc29cf499a0f4c1293f79073e614070472fed4d29042d093e07ebf.png)" :tutorial/id #uuid "6e218979-ac1b-54d9-96aa-977cb17e1bf3" :tutorial/math-academy-id 8580 :tutorial/title "Finding a Common Denominator by Multiplying the Denominators"} :step/id #uuid "306890ff-e120-5250-80b0-44fe5cfefaa3" :step/math-academy-id 134963 :step/next {:db/id 17592186139276}} {:db/id 17592186139276 :step/content {:db/id 17592186138376 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186138133 :question/id #uuid "428ab0f7-87e6-5ca7-8808-e0c5a7763c9f" :question/math-academy-id "e-13739"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "521266c7-b308-5641-98f3-351d1ce63d0e" :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186138702} {:db/id 17592186138949}] :knowledge-point/title "Making a Common Denominator by Multiplying the Denominators"} :step/id #uuid "d75a8f5a-bdca-5e5c-b8c7-03c87bfa5381" :step/math-academy-id 134964 :step/next {:db/id 17592186139277}} {:db/id 17592186139277 :step/content {:db/id 17592186139701 :tutorial/content "In the last few examples, we made a common denominator by multiplying the denominators. Sometimes, this means that we need to compute a large product, which we'd like to avoid if we can.\n\nWhen two denominators have a common factor, it's sometimes easier to find the lowest common multiple, rather than multiplying.\n\nFor example, let's add the two fractions\n\n$$\n\\dfrac{5}{6}\n$$\n\nand\n\n$$\n\\dfrac{3}{8}\n$$\n\nNotice that the denominators ${6}$ and ${8}$ have a common factor of $2$. So let's look at their multiples:\n\n- Multiples of $6: \\quad 6,12,18,{\\color{blue}{24}},30,\\ldots$\n- Multiples of $8: \\quad 8,16,{\\color{blue}{24}},32,40,\\ldots$\n\nThe lowest common multiple is ${\\color{blue}{24}}$. This is the lowest common denominator, too.\n\nTo put\n\n$$\n\\dfrac 5 6\n$$\n\nover a denominator of $24$, we multiply the numerator and denominator by $4$:\n\n$$\n\\dfrac{5}{6} = \\dfrac{5\\times 4}{6 \\times 4} = \\dfrac{20}{24}\n$$\n\nTo put\n\n$$\n\\dfrac 3 8\n$$\n\nover a denominator of $24$, we multiply the numerator and denominator by $3$:\n\n$$\n\\dfrac{3}{8} = \\dfrac{3\\times 3}{8 \\times 3} = \\dfrac{9}{24}\n$$\n\nWe can now add the fractions. We keep the denominator the same, and we add the numerators:\n\n$$\n\\frac{20}{24} + \\frac{9}{24} = \\frac{29}{24}\n$$" :tutorial/id #uuid "9ea81051-d8f6-5494-bcbf-f96bdf982ac8" :tutorial/math-academy-id 8581 :tutorial/title "Adding Fractions Using the Least Common Multiple"} :step/id #uuid "a78448b8-9f3c-57bc-81b7-fe2af685978e" :step/math-academy-id 134968 :step/next {:db/id 17592186139278}} {:db/id 17592186139278 :step/content {:db/id 17592186138377 :knowledge-point/canonical-example {:db/id 17592186138134 :question/id #uuid "a61790a4-96d3-5346-b83e-8f70858ee3b9" :question/math-academy-id "e-13740"} :knowledge-point/id #uuid "05636e74-7815-5a97-92a0-e29c2804d419" :knowledge-point/questions [{:db/id 17592186138730} {:db/id 17592186139046}] :knowledge-point/title "Adding Fractions Using the Least Common Multiple"} :step/id #uuid "1cc6952f-a2ad-539f-9ccf-c9621c7f6433" :step/math-academy-id 134969}] :activity/title "Adding Fractions With Unlike Denominators" :activity/type {:db/id 17592186045463 :db/ident :activity.type/lesson} :db/id 17592186138653} {:db/id 17592186139273 :step/content {:db/id 17592186139699 :tutorial/content "How do we find the value of\n\n$$\n\\dfrac{2}{{\\color{red}{3}}} + \\dfrac 1 {\\color{blue}6}\n$$\n\nwithout using a fraction model?\n\nThe denominators are $\\color{red}3$ and $\\color{blue}6$, which are not the same.
